title: How GLM built its own inference infrastructure
why_read: A detailed engineering account of building custom LLM inference infrastructure at scale is exactly the kind of systems-level detail engineers building AI infra want.
analysis: This piece describes how the team behind GLM (a large language model family) built their own inference serving stack rather than relying entirely on existing frameworks like vLLM or TensorRT-LLM. Such write-ups typically cover batching strategies, KV-cache management, quantization choices, and hardware utilization tricks that materially affect cost and latency at scale. Given 221 comments, it likely sparked substantial technical debate about tradeoffs versus off-the-shelf inference engines. This is genuinely useful for engineers working on production LLM serving systems.
